description: Behavioural evaluation set for the code-ultrareview skill. Cases pin the report shape, target auto-detection across the resolver ladder, the four lenses with their operational definitions, the exclusion/deferral contract (the refuse-to-report discipline), confidence filtering, graceful degradation without a rules baseline, report-only behaviour, and the references-routing for lens detail.

evals.name: produces-canonical-report-shape
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview review the changes on this branch
evals.expected_output: A report matching templates/code-ultrareview.md: a header line with Base, Target, Rule and the rules-baseline status; a Findings table with columns # / Lens / Severity / Location / Conf / Finding / Recommendation ordered by severity then confidence; a Deferred to sibling skills section; What looks good; and a Verdict (Ship / Fix-then-ship / Needs work). No code is modified.

evals.name: auto-detects-dirty-working-tree
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (uncommitted edits present in the working tree)
evals.expected_output: With a dirty tree the skill reviews everything not yet committed: `git diff HEAD` (staged + unstaged) PLUS untracked files (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, read in full) — a brand-new unstaged file is never skipped. Not a branch diff; resolve_base.sh is not consulted in this path. The header states the dirty-tree target.

evals.name: clean-tree-uses-resolver-ladder
evals.expected_output: Clean tree → the skill runs scripts/resolve_base.sh, gets RESULT: base=<merge-base> target=HEAD rule=feature-merge-base, and prints exactly that base/target/rule in the header. An unresolvable RESULT (exit 2) is surfaced verbatim with its hint — the skill does not guess a base.

evals.name: explicit-base-override
evals.expected_output: The skill passes -b origin/main to resolve_base.sh; rule=explicit and auto-detection is skipped. base is resolved to merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) — a diffable ancestor SHA, not the literal ref — so the lenses' two-dot `git diff <base> <target>` is always correct. The header prints that base/target/rule.

evals.name: reads-declared-base-from-rules
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (clean tree; the repo CLAUDE.md declares the source branch is `develop`)
evals.expected_output: Before running the resolver, the skill reads the rule hierarchy, finds the declared source branch (e.g. develop), and passes it via -b. rule=explicit; base is merge-base(develop, HEAD) — a diffable ancestor SHA. This is the skill-layer rung — resolve_base.sh itself never parses rule files.

evals.name: lens1-cites-exact-rule-line
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (a changed file violates a rule written in .claude/rules/)
evals.expected_output: Lens 1 reports the violation with the exact rule line quoted verbatim and a file:line location. Only violations introduced by the diff are reported; pre-existing violations on unchanged lines are not.

evals.name: lens2-flags-drift-against-docstring
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (a function's behavior changed but its docstring/comment still describes the old behavior)
evals.expected_output: Lens 2 reports drift: code no longer matches its own docstring/comment, with file:line and a recommendation to reconcile. Confidence reflects verification.

evals.name: lens4-flags-gap-and-blind-spot
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (new code path added with no test and an unhandled empty-input case)
evals.expected_output: Lens 4 reports a test gap (convention implies a test) and a blind spot (unhandled empty input) as distinct findings with locations. A test that cannot fail when logic changes is also flagged if present.

evals.name: refuses-security-finding-defers-to-sibling
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (the diff is essentially a SQL query built via string concatenation — an injection risk)
evals.expected_output: The skill does NOT report the injection as a finding. It emits a single pointer line under Deferred to sibling skills: a one-liner → /security-review. Staying in lane by construction — security is never a code-ultrareview finding.

evals.name: defers-performance-to-simplify
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (the change adds an O(n^2) loop that could be optimized)
evals.expected_output: Performance/optimization is not a finding. A one-line pointer → /simplify appears under Deferred to sibling skills. Same for pure simplification/dedup observations.

evals.name: graceful-degradation-no-rules-baseline
evals.expected_output: Lens 1 is skipped. The header states `Lens 1 (rules): skipped — no rules baseline found`. Lenses 2–4 still run and the report is produced — the skill remains useful on any repo. The skip is stated, never silent.

evals.name: confidence-filter-drops-below-threshold
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (changes contain one real high-impact bug plus several pedantic nits and a pre-existing issue)
evals.expected_output: The high-impact bug is reported (confidence ≥ 80). Pedantic nits, linter-catchable issues, and the pre-existing issue are scored low and dropped — they do not appear in the Findings table.

evals.name: report-only-bridges-to-apex
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview -s review this branch then fix the issues
evals.expected_output: The skill produces and saves the report to ~/.claude/output/{project}/code-ultrareview/code-ultrareview-{slug}.md and does NOT edit any code. It bridges with the exact command `/apex -f <that absolute path>` for the fix pass (and notes /oneshot takes a description, not a file).

evals.name: routes-to-lenses-reference
evals.prompt: What exactly counts as 'drift' vs a 'blind spot', and what is the confidence cutoff?
evals.expected_output: The skill routes to references/lenses.md for the operational definitions and the 0–100 rubric rather than re-deriving them inline. Answer is concrete (drift = code vs its own doc/sibling pattern; blind spot = unstated assumption; cutoff = 80) and cites the reference.
